title: To Compare, or Not to Compare: On Methodological Practices in Evaluating Social Bias

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating stereotype alignment and discrimination by comparing isolated (single-target) versus forced-choice comparative prompts across tasks including multiple-choice question answering, counterfactual sentence evaluation, toxicity attribution, coreference resolution, and decision-making fairness scenarios.

Assessing model preferences and stereotypes by comparing isolated versus forced-choice comparative prompts on tasks including counterfactual sentence evaluation, decision-making fairness scenarios, and toxicity attribution targeting Black and White demographic groups.

Measuring discrimination and stereotype associations by comparing isolated versus forced-choice comparative prompts on counterfactual sentence pairs, decision-making scenarios, and toxicity attribution targeting Muslim and Christian demographic groups.
